Agni. The god of fire and one of the most ancient and revered deities in Hindu and Vedic tradition.

Agni embodies fire in all its manifestations: the sacrificial flame, the digestive fire within the body, lightning, and the warmth of the sun. He is one of the most prominent deities in the Vedas, worshipped and invoked in nearly every ritual and sacred ceremony since ancient times.

Agni serves as a purifier and divine intermediary between humans and the gods. He accepts ritual offerings from humans and carries them to the gods through smoke and flame. He is depicted with reddish or golden skin and rides a ram as his vahana, his divine mount. He often carries flames and sacred implements in his hands. In some depictions, Agni has four arms and two faces, symbolizing his dual nature as both celestial and earthly fire.

Agni is also associated with digestion, metabolism, and the internal fire that sustains life, known as jataragni. This makes him essential to health and vitality. He is worshipped in Homa fire ritual ceremonies, where offerings are made directly into sacred flames as an act of devotion and gratitude.

In Hindu cosmology, Agni represents the transformative power that breaks down the old to create the new. This makes him essential to both destruction and creation, as he enables change and renewal through his purifying essence.
